# Velxio: Online Circuit and Microcontroller Simulator

> Velxio is a browser-based simulator for electronics and embedded code. You
> place a board and parts, wire them, write the firmware, and run the real
> compiled binary on an emulated chip. A built-in AI agent can do the whole
> job from a description: pick the parts, wire the circuit, write the
> firmware, compile it, run it, read the output and fix what is wrong. Hosted
> at https://velxio.dev. The core is open source (AGPLv3) and can be
> self-hosted with Docker.

## Key facts

- Free plan at https://velxio.dev. No install: it runs in a modern browser.
- Open-core: the simulator is AGPLv3, https://github.com/davidmonterocrespo24/velxio. The hosted site adds paid features on top.
- 55 boards: AVR, ESP32 (Xtensa and RISC-V), RP2040 and RP2350, BBC micro:bit, STM32, Seeed XIAO, and Raspberry Pi running Linux.
- The firmware you run is the compiled firmware (Arduino C++, MicroPython or ESP-IDF, depending on the board).
- Real-time SPICE analog co-simulation with ngspice in WebAssembly: voltages, currents, shorts.
- AI agent that writes firmware, places components, wires them, compiles, runs the simulation and checks the result.
- Supported boards can be flashed from the browser once the project works in the simulator.
- GitHub Sync (Pro): every project save is committed to a repository you choose.
- Embed any public project with an iframe: https://velxio.dev/embed/<id>.

## Plans

| Plan | Price | AI | Projects | Main extras |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Free | $0 | Basic chat, 50 messages a day | public | 150 compiles a day when signed in |
| No AI | $4/mo or $36/yr | none | public, unlisted | the Maker simulator features without the AI |
| Maker | $7/mo or $69/yr | Agent and Tutor, 1,500 credits a day | public, unlisted | STM32 and Raspberry Pi Linux boards, IoT gateway, unlimited compiles |
| Pro | $19/mo or $189/yr | Agent and Tutor, 5,000 credits a day | public, unlisted, private | BOM export, schematic image, GitHub Sync, connect an external agent, My Chips |

AI credits also have a monthly ceiling: 15,000 on Maker and 60,000 on Pro. See https://velxio.dev/pricing for current prices and limits.

## Supported boards

- Arduino and AVR: Uno, Nano, Mega 2560, ATtiny85.
- ESP32: DevKit V1, DevKit-C V4, ESP32-CAM, Wemos Lolin32 Lite, M5Stack Core.
- ESP32-S3: DevKit, XIAO ESP32-S3, XIAO ESP32S3 Sense, Arduino Nano ESP32, M5 Cardputer ADV.
- ESP32-C3 and C6: ESP32-C3 DevKit, C3 SuperMini, XIAO ESP32-C3, ESP32-C6 DevKit, XIAO ESP32C6.
- RP2040 and RP2350: Raspberry Pi Pico, Pico W, XIAO RP2040, XIAO RP2350, Pimoroni Pico Plus 2 W, Badger 2350, Galactic Unicorn, Stellar Unicorn.
- Other Seeed XIAO: SAMD21, RA4M1, nRF52840 Sense, nRF54L15 Sense, MG24 Sense.
- BBC micro:bit V2, alone or on DFRobot boards such as Maqueen Lite and micro:Driver.
- STM32 (Cortex-M3 and M4): Blue Pill, Black Pill, F4 Discovery, Olimex H405, Netduino 2 and Plus 2.
- Linux boards: Raspberry Pi Zero, 1, 2, 3, 4 and 5, and the DFRobot UNIHIKER M10.

STM32 and Linux boards run on Velxio's servers and need a paid plan. A free account gets three 15-minute trial sessions per family (STM32, Raspberry Pi, UNIHIKER).

## Compared with other tools

- **Wokwi**: both run real firmware in the browser. Velxio has an open-source core you can self-host, SPICE analog simulation, and an agent that builds and tests the circuit.
- **Tinkercad Circuits**: aimed at first steps with a small set of boards. Velxio covers ESP32, RP2040, RISC-V, STM32 and Raspberry Pi Linux.
- **Proteus**: a paid desktop program. Velxio runs in the browser and has a free plan.
- **PlatformIO**: a build and debug toolchain. Velxio is a simulator, so a sketch can be tried without hardware.

## Key use cases

- Describe a device in plain language and get a working circuit and firmware, tested in the simulator.
- Learn embedded systems without buying hardware.
- Try Arduino, ESP32, Pico or micro:bit code before flashing a real board.
- Teach: share projects as links or embed them in course pages.
- Check analog behavior: LEDs, RC filters, op-amps and transistors through SPICE.

## Common questions

**Is Velxio free?** There is a permanent free plan with public projects, the in-browser boards, 150 compiles a day for a signed-in account and Basic AI chat. The agent that builds projects is on Maker and Pro.

**Does Velxio require installation?** No. It runs in a modern browser. Self-hosting uses Docker.

**What does the AI agent do?** It reads the circuit and the code of your project, picks and places parts, wires them, writes the firmware, installs libraries, compiles, runs the simulation, reads the serial output and the display, and corrects its own errors. Basic mode only answers questions and shows code in the chat. Tutor mode teaches step by step.

**Is my code private?** Free projects are public. Maker and No AI add unlisted projects (reachable by link only). Pro adds private projects.

**Can I self-host Velxio?** Yes. The AGPLv3 image is published on GitHub Container Registry and Docker Hub. The paid features and the AI agent of velxio.dev are a private overlay and are not part of it.

**Can I embed a project?** Yes, public projects can be embedded with https://velxio.dev/embed/<id>. Projects of free accounts show a "Powered by Velxio" badge.

## License

The open-source core is AGPLv3. The AI agent, billing and the other paid features of velxio.dev are private and are not covered by it.
